rationale: Evidence: iteration 8 (mass 0.4 kg) is the best so far at 690.5. Oval finishes 20/20 (2.41 s), s-bend 20/20 (2.79 s), and slalom 0/20 with progress 0.52, 17 off-track and 3 timeouts. Iteration 8 is the reference because it has the highest score and the best slalom progress so far. Mass 0.5 to 0.4 slowed the oval and s-bend finish times, so mass is not the lever that limits the bends. Slalom failures are still off-track at max_error about 0.06 m, so the remaining limit is turn authority at sharp direction changes. Change, kept to one lever: wheel_track 0.10 to 0.09 m (within the 0.08 to 0.18 range). For the same PWM difference this gives a larger turn rate, which is the same authority gain that the earlier kp increases tried to provide. kp 5.5 and kd 2.5 are unchanged because kp 6.0 with a wider sensor spread (iteration 7) regressed sharply, and kd is near its useful limit. Mass stays at 0.4 since it is at the allowed minimum and reverting it adds no information. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.6 with a few finishes or fewer timeouts, oval and s-bend completion held at 100%, and steering_oscillation at or below about 0.3. Hypotheses: H1, the narrower track raises turn authority at sharp slalom bends, shown by slalom progress and line_loss_events improving. H2, if the narrower track overshoots, steering_oscillation rises above 0.3 and s-bend max_error approaches 0.06, which would mean authority is now too high and wheel_track should go back toward 0.10 with kd raised. H3, if slalom timeouts persist with the same progress, the limit is speed, and base_speed on slalom is the next lever. Next measurements: progress and completion_time for speed versus stability, max_error and line_loss_events for stability, steering_oscillation for damping, control_effort for gain cost, and noise_robustness for margin on held-back tracks.
